query: In pediatric patients with relapsed/refractory ALL, what does the evidence show about CAR-T cell therapy versus blinatumomab for achieving durable remission?
sub_questions: Clinical trials: CAR-T tisagenlecleucel blinatumomab relapsed refractory ALL pediatric
PubMed literature: CAR-T versus blinatumomab pediatric ALL remission durability comparison
Outcomes data: CAR-T blinatumomab pediatric ALL response rates long-term survival
trial_findings: ELIANA trial (tisagenlecleucel, n=75 pediatric r/r ALL): overall remission rate 81%, 12-month event-free survival 50%, 12-month OS 76%. MT103-205 (blinatumomab pediatric, n=93): CR rate 39%, 12-month OS 55%. ALCANTARA (blinatumomab Ph+ ALL): CR 36%. No head-to-head pediatric RCT exists.
literature_findings: Systematic review (8 studies, 2019-2024): tisagenlecleucel shows superior CR rates (81% vs. 39%) but higher severe CRS (77% grade ≥3 CRS). Blinatumomab 2-year follow-up data shows durable responses in 18-25% of complete responders. CAR-T responses more durable at 24 months (relapse-free survival 35-40% vs. 15-20%). Both are bridging strategies to allogeneic SCT in most centres.
outcomes_findings: Paediatric oncology registry (COG/SIOPE, 2019-2024, n=284): tisagenlecleucel 24-month OS 58%, blinatumomab 24-month OS 41% (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.49-0.84, p=0.001). CAR-T associated with higher early treatment-related mortality (8% vs. 1.2%) but superior long-term outcomes. Blinatumomab preferred for Ph+ ALL and CNS disease due to toxicity profile.

contradictions.claim_a: 12-month OS 76% with tisagenlecleucel in r/r ALL
contradictions.claim_b: 24-month OS 58% — suggests significant drop-off in real-world vs. trial, possible patient selection and centre expertise effects

contradictions.claim_a: CAR-T significantly superior to blinatumomab at 24 months (HR 0.64, p=0.001)
contradictions.claim_b: Most expert centres use blinatumomab as bridge to SCT before CAR-T, making direct comparison confounded by treatment sequencing

final_answer: For pediatric r/r ALL, tisagenlecleucel (CAR-T) achieves superior initial remission rates (81% vs. 39%) and more durable responses at 24 months (OS 58% vs. 41%, HR 0.64) compared to blinatumomab. However, a high-severity contradiction exists: trial remission rates (76% OS at 12 months) exceed real-world registry outcomes (58% at 24 months), suggesting significant patient selection in ELIANA. CAR-T carries substantially higher early treatment-related mortality (8% vs. 1.2%) and severe CRS. Blinatumomab is preferred for CNS disease and Ph+ ALL and is widely used as a bridge to SCT. Expert consensus treats both as complementary in sequenced therapy. For most institutions, the choice depends on disease biology, CNS status, toxicity tolerance, and transplant eligibility rather than a single agent being definitively superior.
supporting_evidence: Registry OS advantage for CAR-T: HR 0.64 at 24 months (p=0.001)
Longer durable remission with CAR-T: 35-40% vs. 15-20% relapse-free survival at 24 months
contradicting_evidence: Real-world OS (58%) substantially lower than ELIANA trial OS (76%) — selection bias
Treatment sequencing confounds head-to-head comparison in clinical practice

trace.reasoning: Outcome results sparse; requesting broader outcomes search
